documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: University-wide syllabus language that bans AI for coursework unless an instructor allows it for a specific assignment, leaves the actual rule to each instructor, and supplies three template statements. It requires citation of permitted AI use and treats noncompliance as an academic-integrity matter.
documents.stance_why: The page sets a default ('not permitted to use AI for any course work unless explicitly allowed') but then says 'Class policies related to AI use are decided by the individual faculty' and offers Encouraged, Flexible and Prohibited templates; per the codebook, templates mean delegates.

documents.title: Policies on the use of AI (OURI policy on generative AI in submissions and peer review)
documents.summary: OURI policy for undergraduate research applications and grant peer review. Applicants may use generative AI if they disclose and cite it and stay accountable; reviewers are asked not to upload proposals to AI tools.
documents.stance_why: Applicants are told OURI 'recognizes the value of generative AI' and must 'disclose the extent' of use, so use is allowed with conditions; the reviewer-side limit is narrower.

units.why: Says OURI 'recognizes the value of generative AI in facilitating creativity' in applications, a permissive framing for submissions (P02), with originality still encouraged.
